blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in 2026 in Melbourne?
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed guide to home extension costs in Melbourne, with real examples from Glen Waverley and factors that affect pricing in 2026.
body: Planning a home extension in Melbourne in 2026? Costs vary widely depending on your suburb, the size, and the complexity of the build. In areas like Glen Waverley or Mount Waverley, a single-storey rear extension typically ranges from $80,000 to $150,000 for a basic addition, while larger two-storey projects can easily hit $250,000 or more.

The biggest factor affecting your extension cost in Melbourne is the type of foundation work needed. Many homes in suburbs like Burwood or Box Hill sit on clay or reactive soil, which requires deeper footings and more engineering. That can add $10,000 to $20,000 to the base cost before you even start on framing.

Material prices have also shifted in 2026. Timber framing, steel beams, and cladding all had significant price increases over the past year. Australian-grown hardwood is becoming harder to source, driving up costs for pergolas and decking. If you are planning an outdoor living extension, budget for at least $30,000 to $50,000 for a decent-sized space.

Council fees in Melbourne are another major factor. Suburbs like Camberwell and Doncaster have different planning requirements. A building permit can cost $3,000 to $8,000 depending on the scope, and you may also need a surveyor for boundary adjustments. Skilled Builders Australia includes all these in our fixed-price quote so you know exactly where you stand.

The design phase itself is critical. A detailed architectural plan for an extension in a suburb like Wheelers Hill can cost $5,000 to $15,000, but it saves money long-term because it avoids surprises. We always recommend getting the design right before committing to build — it's cheaper to change a drawing than a wall.

Labour costs in Melbourne have been rising steadily. Skilled builders and project managers are in high demand across the eastern suburbs. A typical extension build takes 12 to 16 weeks from demolition to handover, but that timeline can stretch if you are adding a bathroom or kitchen, which require multiple trades to co-ordinate.

One way to save money is to go for a fixed-price contract from the start. Skilled Builders Australia offers locked-in quotes with itemised costs. No percentage overheads, no vague allowances. Every client in Glen Waverley and beyond gets the same transparent treatment — whether it's a small deck or a full second-storey addition.

To sum up, a home extension in Melbourne in 2026 costs anywhere from $80,000 for a basic room add-on to $300,000 for a premium single storey. The best approach is to book a free on-site consultation with Skilled Builders Australia to get a real number based on your specific block and vision.

blogPosts.title: The Best Time to Pour Concrete in Melbourne's Winter
blogPosts.excerpt: Expert advice on pouring concrete in Melbourne's cooler months, covering curing times, costs, and tips for slabs in suburbs like Doncaster.
body: Pouring concrete in Melbourne during winter is tricky but absolutely manageable if you plan ahead. The key concern is the curing temperature. Concrete sets best between 10°C and 30°C. In Melbourne, winter days can drop below 5°C at night, which slows the curing process and risks cracking if the slab freezes before fully hardening.

In suburbs like Doncaster and Templestowe, where the weather is slightly cooler due to elevation, we often schedule concrete pours for mid-morning after the sun has warmed the ground. We also use insulation blankets and heating cables for larger slabs to keep the curing temperature steady. This adds a bit to the cost — around $500 to $1,500 for a standard driveway or patio slab.

The type of concrete mix matters too. For winter pours in Melbourne, a high-early-strength mix with less water content sets faster and is less prone to frost damage. We also add accelerators to the mix to speed up the chemical reaction. This is standard practice for all our slabs in Box Hill and Camberwell projects.

Another factor to consider is the ground condition. Melbourne's clay soils can get waterlogged during winter rains, which means you need to prepare the sub base properly. We always excavate deeper and use a layer of crushed rock to allow drainage before the concrete goes down. That prevents the slab from shifting or cracking later.

If you are planning a concrete driveway, path, or patio in winter, expect a slightly longer finishing time. The concrete needs to be kept moist during curing, so we cover it with wet hessian or plastic sheeting for at least 7 days. It's not a fast process, but it results in a much stronger, more durable surface that will last for decades.

Cost-wise, a standard concrete slab for a driveway in Melbourne's eastern suburbs ranges from $75 to $110 per square metre for the material alone. Labour adds another $40 to $60 per square metre. Winter pours can have a small premium because of the extra curing materials and labour time, but the difference is usually less than 10%.

At Skilled Builders Australia, we have poured concrete in every condition — rain, cold, heat. Our team in Melbourne knows exactly when to pour and how to protect the work. We always give a fixed price for the slab and include all the winter precautions so you have no surprises.

Bottom line: you can pour concrete in Melbourne any time of year. Just work with a builder who understands the local climate and has the right experience. Book a free consultation with Skilled Builders Australia to discuss your upcoming concrete project.

blogPosts.title: How to Choose the Right Builder for Your Home in Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to vetting builders in Melbourne, from checking licences to reading reviews in Glen Waverley and beyond.
body: Choosing a builder for your home in Melbourne is one of the biggest decisions you'll make. With hundreds of companies advertising across the eastern suburbs, it's easy to get overwhelmed. The key is to focus on three things: experience, communication, and fixed-price contracts. Here is how to vet any builder before signing.

First, always check their licence and insurance. Every registered building practitioner in Victoria has a licence number you can verify on the VBA website. Skilled Builders Australia is fully registered and insured to $20m — that covers public liability, so if something goes wrong on site, you are not out of pocket. Never work with an uninsured builder.

Second, look at their completed projects. A builder who has worked in your suburb before knows the local council rules, the soil conditions, and the typical permit paths. We build across Glen Waverley, Mount Waverley, Box Hill, and beyond, so we know exactly what each area requires. Ask for photos of similar projects to yours.

Third, ask about their quoting process. The best builders give a fixed price after a site visit, not a ballpark over the phone. Skilled Builders Australia gives every client a detailed, itemised quote after our initial consultation. We walk the site, measure, and talk through your vision. That is the only way to get a real number.

Fourth, check reviews from real clients. A good builder will have plenty of testimonials from local homeowners. Look for reviews that mention communication, timeline, and budget — those are the most reliable. In Mount Waverley, our clients regularly praise our daily site updates and single point of contact. That type of feedback is real.

Fifth, make sure the builder offers a warranty. A 7-year structural warranty is standard in Victoria but not all builders are willing to give it. Skilled Builders Australia backs every project with a full warranty, so you have peace of mind long after the build is finished. It's a sign of confidence in their work.

Finally, trust your gut. The best builder for your home in Melbourne is one who listens to you, communicates clearly, and doesn't try to rush you into a decision. Book a free consultation with Skilled Builders Australia and see for yourself how a real local builder operates. We come to you, walk the site, and give it to you straight.
Choosing the right builder means your project runs smoothly, on time, and on budget. Don't settle for less than a fixed-price, insured, local team that stands behind their work.

blogPosts.title: Renovation vs New Build in 2026 — What's Best for Your Block?
blogPosts.excerpt: Compare the costs and benefits of renovating your home versus a knockdown rebuild in Melbourne with real suburb examples and pricing.
body: If you own a home in Melbourne's eastern suburbs, you have probably wondered whether it's better to renovate what you have or knock it down and start fresh. Both options work, but they suit different situations. Here is a detailed comparison to help you decide, with real examples from suburbs like Glen Waverley and Box Hill.

Renovation is often the cheaper path if your existing home has sound structure. In suburbs like Camberwell or Burwood, a full kitchen and bathroom renovation can cost from $50,000 to $80,000 and take 6 to 10 weeks. But if you need to rewire, replumb, or add new rooms, that cost can double quickly. The benefit is that you stay in the home generally and avoid demolition fees.

A knockdown rebuild, on the other hand, is ideal if the existing home is old, poorly laid out, or has structural issues. In Box Hill and Doncaster, where many homes are 50 to 60 years old, the land value is often higher than the house. A full knockdown rebuild can cost $300,000 to $500,000 for a custom home, but you end up with a modern, energy-efficient build that's easier to maintain.

The cost of demolition in Melbourne varies. A standard single-storey house on a flat block can be demolished for around $15,000 to $25,000 including permits and waste removal. But if your site is on a slope or has constraints like easements in Glen Waverley, that figure rises. Skilled Builders Australia includes demolition in our fixed-price quote for full new builds.

Another factor is building standards. New builds in 2026 must meet the latest 7-star energy efficiency standard. That means better insulation, double glazing, and more efficient heating and cooling. Renovations can be exempted from some standards but still need to meet basic compliance. A new build is more predictable for energy costs long-term.

Time frame is also a big difference. A renovation often takes 12 to 20 weeks depending on the scope, while a knockdown rebuild takes 6 to 12 months from concept to handover. If you need to move out during the build, that adds cost — temporary rental in Melbourne's eastern suburbs can run $3,000 to $5,000 a month for a family home.

Skilled Builders Australia offers both renovation and new build services, all under fixed-price contracts. Whether you are refreshing a bathroom in Wheelers Hill or building a brand new home in Mount Waverley, we manage the whole project with a single point of contact. No one passes you between different teams.

The verdict: if your home is structurally sound and you like the location, renovate. If the block is the asset and the house is past its use, a knockdown rebuild is the better investment. Book a free consultation with Skilled Builders Australia and we will walk you through both options on your site with real numbers.
